note: A question functioning as a subordinate clause — subject, object, or in apposition to a noun — within a larger sentence. Distinct from B1's indirekte Rede: it isn't necessarily reporting a question someone actually asked, so it doesn't need Konjunktiv I.

examples.de: Niemand weiß genau, wie die Sache ausgeht.
examples.en: Nobody knows exactly how the matter will turn out.

english: an embedded yes/no question with ob
note: The object of a verb like wissen, sich fragen, or klären can be a whole yes/no question, introduced by ob with the verb at the end — no one needs to have actually asked it aloud.

examples.de: Ich weiß nicht, ob er die Prüfung bestanden hat.
examples.en: I don't know whether he passed the exam.

note: The question word stays exactly where it would be in a direct question; the finite verb moves to the end of the clause.

examples.de: Mir ist nicht klar, warum er das getan hat.
examples.en: It isn't clear to me why he did that.

english: an embedded question as the sentence's subject
note: The whole ob- or W-clause can itself be the grammatical subject of the sentence, not just an object — genuinely new territory beyond B1's reported-question use.

examples.de: Ob das Projekt finanzierbar ist, bleibt fraglich.
examples.en: Whether the project is financially viable remains questionable.

note: An embedded question can also sit in apposition to the noun die Frage — a pattern that reads almost like an extended attribute stating exactly what's in question.

examples.de: Die Frage, ob das Projekt finanzierbar ist, bleibt offen.
examples.en: The question of whether the project is financially viable remains open.

german: Verben mit eingebetteter Frage (sich fragen, klären, herausfinden)
english: verbs that take an embedded question
note: A small set of verbs regularly takes a whole question as their object rather than a noun phrase — sich fragen, klären, herausfinden, prüfen, untersuchen.

examples.de: Die Kommission muss klären, wer für den Schaden haftet.
examples.en: The commission has to establish who is liable for the damage.

english: mood: indicative instead of Konjunktiv I
note: The key contrast with B1's indirekte Rede: Konjunktiv I signals you're reporting someone else's specific utterance and distancing yourself from it. An embedded question that states your own uncertainty, not someone else's words, stays in the plain indicative.

examples.de: Er fragte, ob sie komme. (reported question, Konjunktiv I) — Ob sie kommt, weiß ich nicht. (my own uncertainty, indicative)
examples.en: He asked whether she was coming. (reported question) — Whether she's coming, I don't know. (my own uncertainty)

note: A fixed expression that regularly takes an embedded question as its davon-referent — very common when the outcome genuinely isn't settled yet.

examples.de: Es hängt davon ab, ob die Finanzierung gesichert ist.
examples.en: It depends on whether the funding is secured.

note: Predicate adjectives that name a state of not-yet-knowing regularly introduce an embedded ob-question as their real subject.

examples.de: Es ist ungewiss, ob die Verhandlungen erfolgreich verlaufen.
examples.en: It's uncertain whether the negotiations will be successful.

note: Reports that someone accepted a point, typically after some resistance — softer and more formal than the plain zugeben, common when summarising an argument or interview.

examples.de: Der Minister räumte ein, dass Fehler gemacht wurden.
examples.en: The minister conceded that mistakes had been made.

note: States that someone rejects a claim or accusation as untrue — the natural opposite of einräumen/zugeben.

examples.de: Der Angeklagte bestreitet die Vorwürfe.
examples.en: The defendant denies the accusations.

note: A more direct, neutral synonym of einräumen — states plainly that something is true, without einräumen's connotation of reluctant concession.

examples.de: Sie gab zu, dass sie einen Fehler gemacht hatte.
examples.en: She admitted that she had made a mistake.

note: Reports that someone suggested something indirectly, without stating it outright — the reader or listener has to infer the rest.

examples.de: Er deutete an, dass es bald Veränderungen geben könnte.
examples.en: He hinted that there might be changes soon.

note: Attributes an unstated, often unflattering motive to someone — jemandem etwas unterstellen — noticeably more loaded than andeuten.

examples.de: Man unterstellt ihm, aus Eigeninteresse gehandelt zu haben.
examples.en: He is being accused of having acted out of self-interest.

english: to clarify, to set the record straight
note: Reports that someone corrected a misunderstanding or stated their position unambiguously — often after some confusion or misquotation.

examples.de: Die Sprecherin stellte klar, dass die Entscheidung noch nicht gefallen sei.
examples.en: The spokesperson made clear that the decision had not yet been made.

english: to cast doubt on, to question
note: States that someone questions the truth or reliability of a claim, without necessarily denying it outright the way bestreiten does.

examples.de: Kritiker zweifeln die Zahlen an.
examples.en: Critics are casting doubt on the figures.

english: to suggest, to imply (often subtly or manipulatively)
note: Reports that someone plants an impression without stating it directly — frequently used critically, about advertising or biased framing.

examples.de: Die Werbung suggeriert, das Produkt sei gesund.
examples.en: The advertising suggests the product is healthy.

english: to state, to note (as a fact)
note: A neutral, formal reporting verb — presents something as an established fact, without conceding, doubting, or hinting.

examples.de: Der Bericht konstatiert einen deutlichen Rückgang der Zahlen.
examples.en: The report notes a clear decline in the figures.

note: Reports that someone gave particular weight to one point among several — useful for summarising which part of an argument a source treats as most important.

examples.de: Die Autorin hebt besonders die wirtschaftlichen Folgen hervor.
examples.en: The author particularly highlights the economic consequences.

note: The noun matching einräumen/zugeben — a point given up, often under pressure, in a negotiation or argument.

examples.de: Die Regierung machte im letzten Moment ein Zugeständnis.
examples.en: The government made a concession at the last moment.

note: The noun matching unterstellen — an unstated, often unfair accusation about someone's motive.

examples.de: Das ist eine bloße Unterstellung, keine Tatsache.
examples.en: That's a mere insinuation, not a fact.

note: The noun matching andeuten — something said indirectly, leaving the listener to draw a conclusion.

examples.de: Seine Andeutungen ließen auf einen baldigen Rücktritt schließen.
examples.en: His hints suggested an imminent resignation.

note: The noun matching klarstellen — a statement issued specifically to correct a misunderstanding.

examples.de: Nach der Kritik folgte eine offizielle Klarstellung.
examples.en: An official clarification followed the criticism.

note: The general noun for doubt — Zweifel haben/äußern, an etwas zweifeln; pairs naturally with anzweifeln.

examples.de: An der Richtigkeit der Aussage bestehen erhebliche Zweifel.
examples.en: There are considerable doubts about the accuracy of the statement.

note: Names a suspicion, often in a legal or investigative context — Verdacht schöpfen, unter Verdacht stehen. No natural plural in this sense.

examples.de: Der Verdacht erhärtete sich im Laufe der Ermittlungen.
examples.en: The suspicion was confirmed in the course of the investigation.

note: An emphatic, repeated assurance — often of one's own innocence or good intentions — that the listener may or may not believe.

examples.de: Trotz aller Beteuerungen glaubte ihm niemand.
examples.en: Despite all his protestations, nobody believed him.

note: An educated guess presented as such — explicitly not a confirmed fact, unlike konstatieren's claims.

examples.de: Über die Gründe gibt es nur Mutmaßungen.
examples.en: There is only speculation about the reasons.

note: An unverified claim circulating informally — ein Gerücht verbreiten/dementieren.

examples.de: Das Gerücht verbreitete sich schnell in der Firma.
examples.en: The rumour spread quickly through the company.
